$comment: The English strings of hecpack's pages, the source for every translation. Placeholders are {name}; an object with one/other is a plural, picked with Intl.PluralRules. Translations live in the plugin's data folder (i18n/<lang>.json), written by scripts/i18n.mjs.

preview.title: hecpack preview
preview.subtitle: hecpack {version} preview
preview.nothing: Nothing in the project was changed. This page shows what /init would set up.
preview.initLabel: Set the project up with this selection
preview.tryit: Try it in a throwaway copy of the project
preview.nothingToInstall: Tick a plugin above to get its install command.
preview.docsNote: /hecpack:init reads these and tells you what to carry over and what conflicts with hecpack; nothing is replaced without your word.

info.lite: Session rules, triage, the stack and validation commands; the checker agent.
info.standard: Lite plus the architect loop (analysis before M tasks, review after every task), the thinker and the project map; the designer when the stack has UI, the e2e runner when it has an e2e suite.
info.deep: Standard plus the chain of chats, sub-sessions with a coordinator and model limits per agent.

warn.hooks: The project already runs its own hooks on {events}. With hecpack on, both run and the rules may load twice; keep one source per rule.
warn.agents: The project has its own agents named {names}. hecpack's are hecpack:architect, hecpack:thinker, hecpack:checker; a brief has to name which one it means.
warn.existing: hecpack is already set up here; the diff compares with the current files.

notes.config: level, language, thresholds, models per agent
notes.contextMap: which rules load for which task and agent
notes.claudeMd: one short section pointing to hecpack

preview.installedNote: Plugins and your own skills, agents, commands and hooks, checked against each other and against what hecpack adds. /hecpack:init compares each clash and recommends what to keep; nothing is removed for you.
preview.noConflicts: Nothing here overlaps with each other or with hecpack.

hints.role-clash: Both can start by themselves, so the model may pick either one for the same task. Keep one for this job, or give each a clear part.
hints.role-overlap: These run only when called by name, so they do not get in each other's way; use the one you prefer.
hints.role-together: hecpack calls on these when they are installed: keep them.
hints.hook-clash: Both add to the same moment: rules may load twice and cost tokens on every prompt, or two checks may stop one call.
hints.hook-overlap: Several sources run hooks on this event; check they do not repeat each other.
hints.name-overlap: User and project components share one namespace: the project's one hides the user's.
hints.name-hecpack: A brief has to name hecpack's with its prefix (hecpack:{name}).
hints.mcp-overlap: The same server runs twice and its tools show up twice.

usage.title: Claude Code usage
usage.noMarker: no hecpack setup date (the project has no .claude/hecpack/config.json)
usage.costHint: What the same work would cost on the API, by model.
usage.tokHint: Input, cache writes, cache reads and output together, by model.
usage.cumHint: Running total over the period; the dashed line marks the hecpack setup.
usage.oneSide: The comparison appears once there is usage on both sides of the setup date.
usage.empty: No Claude Code transcripts for this project yet.
usage.gone: deleted by Claude Code, totals kept
usage.yardstick: Subscription plans do not bill per token: the money is a yardstick, not an invoice.

context.title: Context tree
context.sub: What reaches each mode of the main session and each agent at start, and what it may read by link. {map} Built on {date}; tokens are an estimate, characters / 4.
context.noMap: hecpack is not set up here: the page shows what Claude Code loads by itself and the project's own agents.
context.fAllN: in practice a small part is read
context.nReaders: «At start» is loaded with no choice: Claude Code's own files (CLAUDE.md, rules without paths, memory index, agent and skill lists), what the hecpack hook injects for the prompt tag or the agent, and the agent's own instructions. «By link» is what those files point to; it is read only when the task needs it.
context.lClick: click a row for the lists
context.builtin: built-in agent, hecpack hook at start
context.hookOver: The hook injects {chars} characters here, over its {limit}: the rest is named for the agent to read itself. Move a file to a link, or raise parts in context-map.json.
context.nHeavy: A file's tokens times the modes and agents that load it at start. These are the first candidates to shorten, split, or move behind a link.
context.nFiles: For each file: its weight, the modes and agents that load it at start, and those that reach it by link.
context.nRules: Loaded by Claude Code when the session opens a file the globs match: .claude/rules with paths, and CLAUDE.md files in subfolders.
context.nOrph: Agent docs that no mode or agent loads and no file links to. Delete them, or link them from where they matter.
context.nDups: Pairs that share 8-word phrases (the percentage is of the smaller file). Keep one copy and link to it.
context.foot: Built by /hecpack:context, no model involved. Run it again after a change to see the difference.
